## 18.Change, new product and third-party risk

## 18.1Changerisk

Change is a significant source of operational risk. All material change initiatives — system implementations, migrations, organisational restructures, outsourcing transitions and regulatory implementation programmes — require a risk assessment at initiation, at each major stage gate and prior to go-live. The assessment must address risks introduced by the change, risks to business-as-usual during transition, control coverage during parallel running, and the rollback position if the change fails.

Go-live approval requires confirmation that controls have been designed, implemented and tested; that data migration has been reconciled; that affected staff have been trained; that support arrangements are in place; and that a documented rollback plan exists. Go-live may not proceed on the basis that controls will be implemented shortly afterwards.

## 18.2Newproduct approval

chaired by Priyanka S. Raghavan. A material change to sm existing product requires the same approval. The submission must address, No new product, service, market or distribution channel may be launched without approval from the New Product Approval Committee, at minimum: target market, customer need and foreseeable harm; risk assessment across every applicable taxonomy category; legal, regulatory, tax and accounting analysis; financial crime, sanctions and conduct assessment; a data privacy impact assessment where personal data is processed; technology, resilience and third-party dependencies; operational readiness; pricing, profitability and capital consumption; and exit and wind-down arrangements.

Everyapproved product is subjectto post-implementationreviewwithintwelve months,assessing whether the product performedas expected,whether customer outcomesmatched those anticipated,and whether the risk assessment remains valid.

## 18.3 Third-party and outsourcing risk

Third-party arrangements are managed across the full lifecycle: strategy and sourcing, due diligence, contracting, onboarding, ongoing monitoring and exit. Depth of oversight is determined by criticality tier, assessed on the importance of the service, the sensitivity of data shared, the substitutability of the provider and the regulatory classification of the arrangement.

| TIER | DEFINITION | DUEDILIGENCE | ONGOINGOVERSIGHT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier1-Critical | Supports an important business service or processes sensitive data at scale | Full on-site assessment; board- level approval | Annualreassessment;quarterlyservicereview;exitplan tested every 2 years |
| Tier 2-Material | Significant operational dependency without direct customer service impact | Fullremote assessment; evidence-based control review | Annual reassessment;semi-annual servicereview; documented exit plan |
| Tier 3-Standard | Routine supplywith limited dependencyor data access | Questionnaire-based assessment | Biennial reassessment |
| Tier4-Low | Commodity supply,no data access, readily substitutable | Procurement screening only | Contract renewal review |
